title: BlueHarbor Labs - Flow Acceleration weekly sync
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on throughput tuning: continuous batching behavior under production traces, target concurrency, queue depth shaping, and a short troubleshooting session for intermittent tail latency spikes. Agreed to try a prefix cache tweak and increase soft concurrency target; Redwood to send new perf logs and APM traces. Next pilot milestone: validate steady-state 1.8M tokens/day with <=95ms p50 on 2 model shards.
action_items: Alex Chen: upload combined pilot perf logs and raw traces to shared Drive by 2026-07-23
Riley Torres: enable debug-level batching metrics and add batch-size histograms to dashboard by 2026-07-22
Marta Reed: provide a 2-hour production trace sample and request distribution by 2026-07-22
Luis Alvarez: run controlled load test to reproduce tail spike and share script by 2026-07-24
next_steps: Redwood to push a prefix-cache param tweak (increase hot prefix retention) and monitor impact for 48h
Customer to run a 4-hour steady load with new soft concurrency = 48 and report latency percentiles
Schedule a short deep-dive if tail latency persists (invite infra + SE) week of 2026-07-27
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Riley Torres (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Menon (BlueHarbor CTO), Luis Alvarez (BlueHarbor SRE), Marta Reed (BlueHarbor ML Engineer), Connor Yeo (PM)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll run about 30 minutes, quick status then dig into the throughput tuning notes, Riley and I are here to help with any tuning.
[00:22] Priya Menon: thanks Alex, quick context - we've been ramping traffic from that weekend's import job, saw a jump in tokens/sec and then a few tail spikes on p95/p99 last night. want to stabilize before we turn on more flows.
[00:40] Riley Torres: got it. Luis, do you have the spike windows handy? rough timing?
[00:50] Luis Alvarez: yea there's a couple, one around 02:14 UTC and another at 03:51, both correspond to large multi-message chat sessions and some retry storms. i'm not 100% sure if it's the queue depth or KV cold misses.
[01:05] Marta Reed: i also noticed in the trace the batch size collapsed randomly from ~24 down to single-digit and latency jumped. could be continuous-batching not coalescing in those tail periods.
[01:20] Riley Torres: that matches what we've seen when request interarrival becomes bursty; continuous batching groups based on time and length so if there's a short lull the batcher flushes early and you see smaller batches and higher per-token cost and latency variance.
[01:40] Alex Chen: for this pilot our current soft concurrency is 36, hard cap 96, right?
[01:45] Samir Patel: yes that's the config from last week.
[01:51] Priya Menon: correct. we've been conservative on concurrency because we were worried about multi-tenant noise and memory pressure.
[02:05] Riley Torres: two quick levers to try: raise soft concurrency to smooth arrival jitter, and increase the batcher max-wait slightly so the batcher holds a few ms more before flushing. that reduces small-batch events. also prefix/K-V cache retention — if hot prefixes drop out they cause cache misses and a downstream slowdown.
[02:25] Luis Alvarez: okay. what risks with raising soft concurrency? memory, GPU OOM?
[02:32] Jules Park: memory increases linearly with concurrency for KV caches; but our runtime can auto-throttle if host memory crosses thresholds — we've seen safe increases up to 1.4x in similar workloads. still want to ramp slowly.
[02:50] Priya Menon: can we simulate the 03:51 trace to see if raising soft concurrency helps?
[02:58] Riley Torres: yes — Marta, can you share that trace snippet?
[03:05] Marta Reed: i'll drop a 2-hour sample and the request distribution into the shared folder after this call. it's the 03:30-05:30 window.
[03:15] Alex Chen: perfect. quick check on metrics: Riley, what additional telemetry should we enable to diagnose batching anomalies?
[03:22] Riley Torres: enable batch-size histogram, batch flush reason (timer vs capacity), per-batch latency, and a tail-latency allocator that tags requests by prefix key so we can tell if a subset of prefixes are causing the pileups. also KV hit/miss by prefix.
[03:42] Luis Alvarez: we currently only have average batch size and overall p50/p90. i'll enable the histograms — should be low overhead?
[03:48] Riley Torres: low; it's mostly counters and a small histogram overhead. we'll add that to the dashboard.
[04:00] Connor Yeo: small question on fallback behavior: if the primary model backpressure trips, do you auto-fallback to a smaller model? we saw docs mention fallback policies but not sure how it's configured.
[04:12] Jules Park: yes we support model-variant fallback. in this pilot we haven't enabled automatic fallback — it's a config at the routing layer; we can enable a canary fallback to a quantized variant if you'd like. tradeoff is slight quality delta.
[04:30] Priya Menon: we'd prefer predictable latency over small quality loss during surges. quantify that delta?
[04:36] Jules Park: from our benchmarks the quantized variant increases answer delta on niche prompts by measurable but usually acceptable %, you'll get specifics in the quantization report we'll share.
[04:50] Alex Chen: back to tuning plan: propose these immediate steps — 1) raise soft concurrency from 36 to 48 for 48 hours, 2) bump batcher max-wait from 8ms to 12ms, 3) adjust prefix cache hot retention from 300s to 900s for pilot scope. any objections?
[05:15] Priya Menon: no objections, but we want to be able to roll back quickly.
[05:19] Alex Chen: rollback policy is immediate via control plane toggle; we'll also push a guardrail to auto-lower concurrency if memory >85%.
[05:28] Luis Alvarez: good. question: how will we measure success? what pass/fail criteria?
[05:34] Samir Patel: suggested pass: steady-state throughput hits 1.8M tokens/day with p50 <= 95ms and p95 <= 420ms over a 4-hour steady load.
[05:46] Priya Menon: ok that's sensible.
[05:50] Riley Torres: we also want to watch per-prefix tail percentiles and batch-size percentiles to ensure batching improved.
[06:02] Marta Reed: for the tail latency we saw occasional retries from the app layer that amplified the problem. should we add request shaping on the client side?
[06:12] Jules Park: yes client-side backoff and idempotency will reduce retry storms; but we also can set rate-limits and shaping at the routing layer in Redwood to smooth bursts.
[06:25] Luis Alvarez: i'll coordinate with our app team to implement exponential backoff in the next deployment.
[06:30] Alex Chen: great. now some quick troubleshooting notes from last night's spike — Riley, you saw a cold KV miss pattern?
[06:38] Riley Torres: there were periodic patterns where hot prefixes fell out of cache after ~5 minutes of inactivity. our default eviction was too aggressive for this access pattern. increasing retention should reduce misses and the associated upstream work.
[06:50] Priya Menon: how invasive is the prefix retention change? any config restarts?
[06:55] Jules Park: it's runtime-config only; no restart required. we'll apply at the model shard level.
[07:05] Alex Chen: timeline — we aim to apply config changes in the next 24 hours, run a 4-hour steady load tomorrow morning (BlueHarbor to run) and then reconvene Friday for results. do those timelines work?
[07:18] Priya Menon: yes Friday works, prefer morning.
[07:22] Marta Reed: one more ask — can Redwood send an APM trace correlation (span IDs) so we can align app traces to model spans? it's hard to join without shared IDs.
[07:33] Riley Torres: yes we'll attach correlation IDs and examples of how to map them.
[07:40] Alex Chen: ok wrapping up — recap action items and owners. Samir, i'll share the perf doc and update CRM with the new milestone.
[07:50] Samir Patel: noted.
[07:55] Priya Menon: thanks all.
[08:00] Alex Chen: thanks folks, we'll follow up in the channel and send the config diffs.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcript contains imperfect ASR substitutions ("K-V cash" etc), periodic speaker confusion around 03:00-04:00 where Speaker labels may be shifted by one turn in the raw export.
